analysis:
All five units are test-only changes: SSDPrefixCacheTests.swift (windowed sidecar tests, donation outcome tests, write-behind bound helpers) and SSDSharedProcessCheckpointTests.swift (new queuedWritesStayInsideHostLedger test at head lines 147-189). No production source changed in the supplied evidence, so no control was weakened and no new attack surface was added.

Security relevance to T-041 (A-001):
- sidecarHeaderHidesPosition (SSDPrefixCacheTests.swift ~4430-4495) asserts the DBK3 plaintext metadata carries no absolute token position, only a keyed windowBaseTag commitment. It also checks that windowTag is in a separate HMAC domain from the block tag, and that windowKind is the only added plaintext discriminator. This is consistent with the T-041 posture that nothing prompt-derived beyond the keyed lookupTag may be added to the plaintext AAD. The tests pin the property; they do not change it.
- corruptSidecarDegradesToReplay checks fail-closed behaviour: a corrupted sidecar is unlinked and de-indexed, and block adoption still stands.
- donationRefreshesReusedSidecars checks that sidecars slide the TTL together with their blocks.
- sidecarsNeverStarveTheBlocks checks that the write-endurance bucket funds required blocks before optional sidecars.
- disabledByDefault and donorSeamIsSilentWhenDisabled confirm the sidecar feature is off by default (SSDPrefixCachePolicy.windowSidecarEnabled).
- The host-ledger test checks that queued writes keep their reservations, so the host memory ledger binds before the job bound. It also checks that charged bytes return to 0 after close.

Open question for the next pass: the production sidecar and SSDWriteBehind sources are not in this batch. The windowed-sidecar feature and the TB-003 plaintext-header claim in T-041 should be checked against the real SSDBlockStore and SSDLookupKeys implementation, since the tests presume them. The T-041 definition does not yet mention window sidecars (a documentation drift candidate).
